surface_mechanism_description: Alkylaluminum hydride such as chemically stable dimethylaluminium hydride (DMAlH) formed near the exit of the cracking tube by the reaction between DMA and hydrogen carrier gas are supplied to the substrate. H is thought to be easily dissociated on the surface due to catalytic reaction with As compared to methylradical. As a result, DMA is chemisorbed to a surface As atoms. Another is that DNA or MMA directly reach the surface and are chemisorbed.
evidence: There are two possible mechanisms for realizing ALE. One is that alkylaluminum hydride such as a chemically stable dimethylaluminium hydride (DMAlH) formed near exit of the cracking tube by the reaction between DMA and hydrogen carrier gas are supplied to the substrate. H is thought to be easily dissociated on the surface due to catalytic reaction with As compared to methylradical. As a result, DMA is chemisorbed to a surface As atoms. Another is that DNA or MMA directly reach the surface and are chemisorbed.
